# OpenLoop API

> OpenLoop automates AI-agent workflows. This is the machine-readable guide to
> the HTTP API behind the web UI at /. Base URL: http://localhost:54321
> Everything is scoped to an INSTANCE — the absolute path of the project folder
> the openloop worker runs in, URL-encoded.
> Example: /api/instances/%2Fhome%2Fme%2Fapp
> The list always includes one synthetic "global share" instance; address it
> the same way as any other.

## Quick start
1. GET /api/instances                    → find your instance `path`
2. GET /api/instances/:id/workflows      → see what it can run
3. POST /api/instances/:id/manual-workflows  { "workflow_id": "...", "ask": "..." }
4. GET /api/instances/:id/manual-workflows/:runid  → poll until status != "running"

    curl -s localhost:54321/api/instances | jq '.instances[0].path'

## Conventions
- :id = encodeURIComponent(instanceFolderPath). Write bodies are JSON
  (Content-Type: application/json). List/get responses are JSON. Knowledge
  file bodies are raw text. Success: DELETE → 204, instance lifecycle → 200.
- Every route is under /api/instances/:id/... .

## Endpoints

Instances — list & lifecycle
  GET    /api/instances               → { instances:[{ path, parentPath?, state?,
                                  manualActive, manualCompleted, configEnabled?,
                                  processRunning?, isGlobalShare }] }
                                  state = { lastLoopAtUnixMs, activeRunningWorkflows,
                                            inactiveWorkflows }
                                  (configEnabled/processRunning are absent on the
                                  global-share instance.)
  POST   /api/instances/:id/launch    → start the worker for a folder   (200)
  POST   /api/instances/:id/stop      → kill the running process        (200)
  POST   /api/instances/:id/disable   → stop auto-loading on boot       (200)
  DELETE /api/instances/:id/delete    → remove service registration     (200)
  DELETE /api/instances/:id           → unload                          (200)

Personas — CRUD
  GET    /api/instances/:id/personas        → { personas:[{ id, name, role, avatar? }] }
  GET    /api/instances/:id/personas/:pid   → { name, role, about, task, avatar?, agent? }
  POST   /api/instances/:id/personas        body { id?, name?, role?, about?, task?,
                                                   avatar?, agent? }
  PUT    /api/instances/:id/personas/:pid   body: any subset (partial merge)
  DELETE /api/instances/:id/personas/:pid   → 204

Workflows — CRUD
  GET    /api/instances/:id/workflows       → { workflows:[{ id, name, desc, ask }] }
  GET    /api/instances/:id/workflows/:wid  → { name, desc, every_secs, agent, ask, levels }
  POST   /api/instances/:id/workflows       body { id?, name?, desc?, every_secs?, agent?,
                                                   ask?, levels? }  (id ∈ [A-Za-z0-9_-])
  PUT    /api/instances/:id/workflows/:wid  body: any subset (partial merge)
  DELETE /api/instances/:id/workflows/:wid  → 204
  GET    /api/instances/:id/workflows/:wid/runs  → { workflow_id, runs:[id] }

Manual runs — launch a workflow by hand, then watch it
  POST /api/instances/:id/manual-workflows/validate  body { workflow_id, ask? }
                                              → { valid, errors[] }      (422 if invalid)
  POST /api/instances/:id/manual-workflows     body { workflow_id, ask? }
                                              → { id, workflow_id, ask, started_at,
                                                  status:"running", output }
  GET  /api/instances/:id/manual-workflows     → { workflows:[...] }
  GET    /api/instances/:id/manual-workflows/:runid  → status ∈ running|completed|failed
  DELETE /api/instances/:id/manual-workflows/:runid  → 204
  State is RAM-only (lost on restart); completed entries are swept ~1h later.
  `ask` is optional and defaults to the workflow's saved ask.

Logs — execution history (paginated: offset, count)
  GET /api/instances/:id/logs/personas?personaId=&offset=0&count=5
                                       → { logs[], stats:{ [pid]:{errors,success,total} },
                                           offset, count, total }
  GET /api/instances/:id/logs/workflows/:wid?offset=0&count=5
                                       → { logs[], offset, count, total }
  GET /api/instances/:id/logs/sessions/:session
                                       → { levels[], logs[] }  (full waterfall of one run)
  entry: { success, took, started_at(ms), ended_at(ms), id, workflowId, personaId?,
           agent, session?, level?, msg:{ input, output, parents:[{ id, text }] } }

Knowledge — per-persona plain-text file store
  GET    /api/instances/:id/personas/:pid/knowledge         → { files:[String] }
  GET    /api/instances/:id/personas/:pid/knowledge/**path  → raw text (text/plain)
  PUT    /api/instances/:id/personas/:pid/knowledge/**path  body = raw text → 200
  DELETE /api/instances/:id/personas/:pid/knowledge/**path  → 204
  (** = catch-all sub-path. ../ traversal is rejected with 403.)

## Core models
- Persona : { name, role, about(=system prompt), task, avatar?, agent? }
- Workflow: { name, desc, every_secs, agent, ask, levels:[[String]] }
- every_secs: -1 = run once at startup · 0 = manual only · 1 = continuous
              (next run scheduled right after finishing) · >1 = repeat every N s
- levels entries: a personaId | ":workflowId" (nested workflow) |
                  "id:rw" (force read-write).
  A level with ≥2 personas runs READ-ONLY. A single-persona level may be RO or RW.
  The last level always writes; each level sees only the previous level's output
  + the ask. Many minds analyze, then one hand acts.

## More
- Human docs (concepts, not endpoints): /docs.html
- Full trace of one run: /api/instances/:id/logs/sessions/:session
